duties.plain: 4. In these directions, unless the context otherwise requires, the terms here must bear the meanings assigned to them below: (1) 'Debtor company' means any company to which the NBFC currently has or previously had a loan or investment exposure (excluding equity instruments) anytime during the preceding twelve months.

Explanation: The 'business of financial services' must include: (i) the forms of business enumerated in clauses (a), (c), (d), (e) of sub- Section (1) of Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and notified under clause (o) of sub-Section (1) of Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

6. The Board of an NBFC intending to undertake distribution of mutual fund products must approve a comprehensive policy regarding undertaking mutual funds distribution, customer appropriateness and suitability as well as grievance redressal mechanism in addition to fulfilling the other terms and conditions as prescribed in paragraphs 50 and 51.
7. An NBFC's investment policy must have suitable provisions governing its investments in an AIF Scheme, compliant with extant law and regulations.
8. An NBFC must not individually contribute more than 10 percent of the corpus of an AIF Scheme.
9. The aggregate contribution by all regulated entities (REs) in any AIF Scheme must not be more than 20 percent of the corpus of that scheme.

10. Where an NBFC contributes more than five percent of the corpus of an AIF Scheme that has downstream investment (excluding equity instruments) in a debtor company of the NBFC, the NBFC must be required to make 100 percent provision to the extent of its proportionate investment in the debtor company through the AIF Scheme, subject to a cap equivalent to NBFC's direct loan and / or investment exposure to the said debtor company.

16. An NBFC must obtain prior approval of the RBI for opening of subsidiary / joint venture or undertaking investment abroad.
The application from the NBFC seeking No Objection must be considered subject to compliance with general and specific conditions prescribed in paragraphs 17 and 18.

17. An NBFC, intending to open a subsidiary, joint venture, or undertake investment abroad, must comply with the following general conditions: (1) Investment in non-financial service sectors must not be permitted.
The overseas investment in a single entity, including its stepdown subsidiaries, by way of equity or fund-based commitment must not be more than 15 percent of the NBFC's owned funds.
All approvals for investment abroad must be subject to this condition.
An NBFC proposing to establish a subsidiary abroad must comply with all the conditions as stipulated in paragraph 16 above.
In addition, the following conditions must apply: (1) The parent NBFC must not extend implicit or explicit guarantee to or on behalf of such subsidiaries.
However, companies undertaking activities such as financial consultancy and advisory services with no significant assets must not be considered as shell companies.
(9) All the operations of the subsidiary abroad must be subject to regulatory prescriptions of the host country.
19. All overseas investments by an NBFC, other than in subsidiaries, must be governed by the same guidelines to subsidiaries established abroad, as specified in these Directions.
